newsitem.title: USA: KC Fed's Hoenig sees more consolidation in banking.
newsitem.headline: KC Fed's Hoenig sees more consolidation in banking.

text.p: President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Thomas Hoenig said Thursday he expected recent consolidation in the banking industry to continue due to advancements in technology.
Addressing a seminar sponsored by the Missouri State Treasurer here, Hoenig said, "We're seeing a very significant consolidation of the banking industry.
"This consolidation is really occurring for a couple of reasons. One (reason) is we have an enormous advance in technology," allowing investment managers to develop new products and instruments.
In addition, Hoenig said advances in communications are enabling the investment community to inform potential investors of such new products.
Speaking to reporters after the session, Hoenig said the local job market was tight, reflective, in his opinion, of the rest of the nation.

"We are finding the (local) jobs market tight, both at the entry level and especially for high-tech areas, and it's very similar, I think, to much of the rest of the country," the Kansas City Fed chief said.
Asked if there were any great anomalies between the Tenth U.S. Economic District and the remainder of the country, Hoenig said he did not know of any.
"Our manufacturing is good; as I said our demand for labor is strong ... and agriculture is doing reasonably well," he said.
